narratives.Overview:
## Parent

#4125 (filed 2026-09-02). This is a current-date refile with a new consumer reproduction, not a new root cause.

## Blocked by

Grok Build host contract. Public `xai-org/grok-build` has issues disabled.

## Do not implement in Directive

The reader half shipped on #3873. What remains is the same host spawn-environment miss as #4125: `deft-hook` is a sibling process and does not receive `GROK_SESSION_ID`.

## Problem

On 2026-09-15, a Grok Build mutation session on Windows (`deftai/FairMark`, P1-15 Fly deploy) hit the occupancy self-deadlock end to end:

1. `deft session:start` claimed occupancy as `host:grok:v1:<id>`.
2. Immediate `Write` / `search_replace` denials: worktree occupied by **that same session id**, `no recorded write`.
3. `occupancy:heartbeat` from the agent shell succeeded (CLI sees the owner). Tool-call writes stayed denied.
4. First `python -c` file write via Shell succeeded; a later compound PowerShell here-string was denied as `Shell write dest is not reconstructable (compound command)`.
5. `occupancy:release` unblocked occupancy. The next `Write` then hit the intended active-xBRIEF gate (#810). Creating/activating a dummy scope xBRIEF unblocked product writes.

Wall clock from mutation intent to first allowed `Write` was ~11 minutes of gate fighting, not product work.

Matches #4125: the write gate treats the lease holder as a stranger and names the holder back at them.

## Unblock when

Grok Build injects `GROK_SESSION_ID` into hook processes (same id as the agent shell) and does not leak a foreign `DEFT_SESSION_ID`. Then re-measure a real Edit/Write on Windows Grok Build.

## Non-goals

- Fail-open on missing identity (#3611 / #3156).
- Further Directive identity-transport work; that shipped on #3873.
- Treating a CLI `DEFT_SESSION_ID` export as the fix.

Refs #4125, #3873, #3954, #4020, #4028.

## 1. Owner resolution is not dest occupancy

class: blocks-the-design

Evidence, re-run at dest SHA 650ea08e71d9b856ec9c01949066f9e0824fde35 (HEAD):

- Dest occupancy already treats a Grok process as Grok when argv host is claude. `isGrokHookProcess({ GROK_HOOK_EVENT: "PreToolUse" })` is true. `appliesGrokSpawnDestContract({ host: "claude", toolName: "Write", environ: { GROK_HOOK_EVENT: "PreToolUse" } })` is true. Vitest passed: dispatcher-spawn-dest "applies Grok dest and emits no envelope rewrite when --host is claude and GROK_HOOK_EVENT is set". Native Grok deposit is still `--host grok` (agent-hooks.test).
- Occupancy owner resolution is a different surface. `GROK_HOOK_EVENT` appears in readonly.ts / spawn-dest tests only, not in host-session-identity.ts or occupancy.ts. `resolveHookHostIdentity("claude", { session_id }, dualEnv-with-GROK_SESSION_ID)` still returns provider claude. The canonical id is `host:claude:v1:MDFhMGE2NmEtOWI4Ni03NDIzLTgyZjktOThkOTdjZjViMDk5`, the same string as comment 5687097563.
- Dual-host mint-refusal, no `GROK_SESSION_ID`: env `{ GROK_AGENT, GROK_HOOK_EVENT, CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID }` yields `detectDeclaredIdentityHosts` = ["claude", "grok"]. The only print companion is the Claude owner. `resolveOccupancySessionClaim` is refuse-mint and tells the caller to re-run with `--session-id=host:claude:v1:MDFhMGE2NmEtOWI4Ni03NDIzLTgyZjktOThkOTdjZjViMDk5`. That is the NoteTechnic claim command.
- `GROK_HOOK_EVENT` alone under `--host grok` is identity missing: "grok hook process environment omits GROK_SESSION_ID."
- 186 tests passed on readonly, dispatcher-grok-identity, host-session-identity, occupancy-mint-refusal, host-session-owner.

Failure mode: a Grok process on a dual-host tree is steered to claim a Claude owner, then the write gate treats that holder as a stranger. Injecting `GROK_SESSION_ID` into the hook sibling does not change `--host claude` owner resolution. Shared occupancy.json then carries a Claude bearer for a Grok session; disabling Claude hooks to proceed breaks the other host on the same repo.

Disposition: the lean cannot bind as "do not implement / same miss as #4125" for the whole issue. Do not invent a third dest-occupancy copy (#4272 already owns that override). The remaining Directive surface is occupancy owner resolution and #4431 mint-refusal companion selection, adjacent to the #4409 argv `--host` remainder. FairMark's grok-claim then stranger-deny can stay #4125-shaped; NoteTechnic cannot.

## 2. occupancy-occupied does not record hook --host

class: sharpens-framing

Evidence: commands.md child `--host` remainder (#4409) and dispatcher-grok-identity tests print `hook --host <flag>` on occupancy-identity-conflict and occupancy-identity-unavailable only. FairMark (issue body) and NoteTechnic (comment 5687097563) quote occupancy-occupied, the same session id, and no recorded write. That path names the lease holder and does not print the child argv host.

Failure mode: a bind that treats both field notes as one miss, or as proof of `--host claude` Write, is reading a message that cannot show the argv.

Disposition: keep FairMark as #4125-shaped only if the record says occupancy-occupied notes do not observe `--host`. A re-measure that needs argv must quote an identity-conflict / identity-unavailable line or capture the child argv.

## 3. Reader half on #3873 is present

class: footnote

`HOST_ENV_IDENTITY_VARIABLES` is ["GROK_SESSION_ID"]. Claim with that variable binds `host:grok:v1:…` and host-authoritative claim beats leftover `DEFT_SESSION_ID`. Native deposit is `--host grok`. That is the shipped reader. It does not decide the owner-resolution split above.

## Injection / swarm lens

The target changes identity, hooks, occupancy, and dual-host shared state. Dest occupancy already special-cased Grok process identity when argv host is claude or cursor (#4272). Owner resolution did not. Occupancy stays cooperative routing, not authentication. Fail-open on missing identity stays out of scope (#3611 / #3156).

## Road not taken

Steelmanned close: inject `GROK_SESSION_ID` into the CLI and the hook sibling; FairMark Write admits; mint-refusal never fires; no Directive change.

What flips it: (1) mint-refusal still suggests Claude whenever `GROK_AGENT` is set and `GROK_SESSION_ID` is absent — `GROK_HOOK_EVENT` can be present without the session id (measured); (2) `--host claude` owner resolution ignores `GROK_SESSION_ID` even when present (measured). Host injection does not collapse those two.

## 1. The cite covers one of three clauses in the denominator

class: blocks-the-design

Evidence: the write-back gate stamp names three clauses — (a) a Grok process presents a Claude bearer id, (b) native Write deadlocks on that id, (c) a Grok agent disables Claude hooks to proceed. Lean 5689655075's plain-English says "so a Grok process does not claim or get told to re-run as `host:claude:v1`. That is P1." That sentence is clause (a) alone, restated as the whole pain. Under `### Pain coverage`, "the latest Stop 1 write-back owns the denominator" and "a superseding warrant is a new Stop 1, not last-writer prose elsewhere on the thread." No Stop 1 write-back after 5688609916 exists at or below this ceiling (thread: 5687097563, 5688609916, 5688730962, 5688748469, 5688749978, 5688751457, 5689655075). So the lean narrowed the denominator on the lean, and the same grok-4.6 parent authored both ends of that narrowing.

Failure mode: `evaluateCompletedArcRecord` reads one cited id against one declared id and returns covered. It does not grade relief (ADR-005), so a 1-of-3 relief passes as full coverage and the arc clears toward ingest on a pain whose costly clauses are untouched. The self-attested non-self-arbitration note records the conflict; it does not discharge it.

Disposition consequence: the cite as posted is not supportable against this denominator. Either Stop 1 re-issues with the clauses split into separate pain ids and the lean cites only the relieved one, or this lean carries `does-not-relieve` / `operator-deferred` for P1 in place of the relief cite.

## 2. Owner resolution changes which id the lease carries, not whether the hook can present one

class: blocks-the-design

Evidence: clause (b) is the deadlock. Both field notes end at the same wall, and it is not the owner's host.

- FairMark (issue body, steps 1-2) claimed `host:grok:v1:<id>` — already Grok-shaped — and native Write was still denied as occupied by *that same session id*, `no recorded write`. Correct owner resolution was present and did not admit the write.
- A2: the Grok hook sibling omits `GROK_SESSION_ID`, so it presents nothing. `dispatcher.ts` denies that state as `occupancy-identity-unavailable` (at the occupancy gate, and again in `recheckOccupancyBeforeWriteAllow`). A deny, not a degraded allow.
- C2: when `GROK_SESSION_ID` *is* published, the claim already resolves to `host:grok:v1:…` at dest today. The only environment where a Grok process is steered to a Claude owner is the one where `GROK_SESSION_ID` is absent — which is exactly the case the Bound remedy's last item hands back: "Missing GROK_SESSION_ID on a Grok-declared process is identity-unavailable on Grok, not a Claude owner."
- C3 measures that handed-back state: `refuse-mint` with `suggestedSessionId: null` and a `<host-published-id>` placeholder.

Failure mode: apply the remedy to the reported NoteTechnic repro and the operator moves from "claim under a Claude bearer, then get denied at Write" to "cannot claim at all, with no runnable id in the message." Apply it to FairMark and nothing changes; the remedy says so ("FairMark occupancy-occupied can stay #4125-shaped"). The ~11 minutes of gate fighting in the issue body is clause (b), and no item in the Bound remedy shortens it. The single open issue in the remedy's reference set is #4125, which is blocked on a host whose tracker has issues disabled.

Disposition consequence: clause (b) is deferred, not relieved. `operator-deferred: P1 #4125` is the available closed form and cites a different issue id, which is legal — but per `### Pain coverage` it stays an unresolved ADR-006 marker (`unresolved-pain-audit`) until a critic targets it, and "Dual-stop spent plus unrelieved pain prints halt-for-human or Handoff, not ingest." Lean 5689655075 already carries an operative `Spec-path` token, so a corrected cite of either closed form satisfies Handoff print condition 1. That is the printed consequence; the dispatch call is the operator's.

## 3. The dual-host hooks clause closes on prose, not a control

class: sharpens-framing

Evidence: clause (c) of P1 is an operator disabling Claude hooks to get Grok working. The Bound remedy answers it with "Dual-host: keep Claude hooks installed. Do not recover Grok pain via `policy:disable-host-hooks --host claude`." At dest, `disableHostHooks` (`packages/core/src/policy/host-hooks.ts:182`) validates only that the host is in `HOOK_HOSTS` and that `--confirm` was passed; it prints a capability-cost disclosure and persists `hostHooks.claude=false`. There is no dual-host predicate, no refusal when the disabled host is the only one with a resolvable owner, and no occupancy-side read of the flag on the deny path. The prohibition lives in a GitHub comment; nothing in the tree observes it.

Failure mode: an operator who hits finding 2's dead end reaches for the one command that visibly changes behaviour, `--confirm` clears it, and the audit log records it after the fact. Clause (c) then occurs exactly as the write-back predicts, with the remedy nominally in force.

Disposition consequence: state this item as a mechanism or drop the clause from the relief claim. Per the critic method, a safety case that ends at "the contract says not to" is unresolved unless a deterministic control is named — for instance a refusal in `disableHostHooks` when `detectDeclaredIdentityHosts` reports a second declared host, reusing the predicate B1 already exercises. I am not claiming that specific control is the right one; I am claiming the item names none.

## 4. First-ship of the #4431 companion selection names a closed, shipped selector

class: sharpens-framing

Evidence: #4431 is CLOSED (`xbrief/completed/2026-09-11-4431-...`), #4409 CLOSED, #4272 CLOSED; only #4125 is open. The companion selector already exists and shipped: `uniquePrintCompanion` (`occupancy.ts:635`) over `PAYLOAD_HOST_PRINT_COMPANIONS` (`host-session-owner.ts`), and it is what produces the Claude suggestion in C1 — it returns the single printable companion, and grok has none (B2), so on `["claude","grok"]` the Claude id is unopposed.

Failure mode: the remainder is a change to a shipped selection rule, not a first ship. A builder harvesting this heading either reopens a closed issue or reads the item as already delivered, and in both cases the one-line rule change is never written down.

Disposition consequence: restate the item against the shipped symbol and name the rule it needs — the disposition is unchanged, the harvest target is not.

## 5. The recut changed the cite, not the remedy

class: footnote

The Bound remedy on 5689655075 is byte-identical to the one on superseded lean 5688748469 apart from one trailing blank line (`diff` over both bodies). The recut's whole delta is the relief cite plus the chip removal. Nothing in the remedy was re-scoped in response to the pain cite, which is why findings 1-3 land on the cite rather than on any new text.

## Injection / swarm lens

Fires: the target changes identity, occupancy, hooks, worktrees and dual-host shared state.

The security-shaped half of the remedy is real and worth keeping. `occupancy.json` on a dual-host tree is shared state, and C1 currently steers a Grok process to write a Claude bearer into it, then hands the operator that id as an explicit `--session-id` argument. `PAYLOAD_HOST_PRINT_COMPANIONS` is commented as print-only precisely because `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is shell-reachable and inherited by child sessions — the #4066 class. The refuse-mint suggestion is the one path that moves that value out of print-only and into a claim the operator types. Removing the cross-host bearer from shared occupancy is a defensible improvement on its own terms.

It is not P1 relief. Occupancy stays cooperative routing, not authentication (unchanged here), and the write gate still denies on identity-unavailable either way. The lens supports the remedy; it does not support the cite.

## Road not taken

I chose between reading P1 as the write-back's three-clause conjunction and reading it as the lean's one-clause restatement. Taking the lean's reading, the relief cite is true as posted, findings 1-3 collapse, and this audit returns clean.

What flips me back: `### Pain coverage` gives the denominator to the latest Stop 1 write-back and says in terms that a superseding warrant is a new Stop 1, not prose elsewhere on the thread. The lean is prose elsewhere on the thread.
